title: Beginner's Guide: MapleStory Classic World
intro: Your first hours in MapleStory Classic World: Maple Island, first job, AP, potions that stretch your mesos, and quests worth doing to level 35.

blocks.p: [[img:d6e564683a59cd.png]]
Your goals on Maple Island:

ul: Talk to every NPC. Most hand out a one-quest, small-EXP-and-an-item reward.

**Grab the Green Relaxer chair.** It's the reward from Pio's quest below, and this is the only place you can get it. If too many players are camping Pio's boxes, buy the Sky-blue Wooden Chair instead.

By the time you finish all the beginner quests on Maple Island, you'll likely be lv 8. Shanks at the dock sails you to Lith Harbor for 300 mesos once you reach level 7. **The boat is one-way.** Hand in every Maple Island quest before you board.

blocks.p: All 10 Maple Island quests (chains counted once, EXP summed across steps), straight from the quest tracker:

table: Please bring this letter to Lucas

blocks.p: **Plan your AP for the job you want.** You place your first 9 AP on the character creation screen, so pick your class before you make your character. STR gives a Beginner stronger basic attacks than INT does. Putting AP into INT for Magician can mean slower kills before advancement, but your AP does not reset when you take your first job. Keep the points in your future job's primary stat.

blocks.h2: Pick Wooden Club, then Razor at level 5

blocks.p: [[img:9eab57ead0d224.png]]Choose the Wooden Club at character creation. It has 19 W.ATK; the Sword and Hand Axe have 17. Club attacks one tier slower than Sword or Hand Axe, but across levels 1 to 4, the Club reaches the useful damage breakpoints more often.
Against a level 1 Snail with all 9 creation AP in STR (13 STR, 4 DEX, 4 INT, 4 LUK), each starter weapon needs:
Club matches or beats both 17 W.ATK weapons on minimum, average, and maximum damage for **every class path**. Its higher damage can save a hit when it crosses a monster's HP threshold.
[[img:eb1de53f04fc53.png]]**At level 5, switch to Razor.** Its 23 W.ATK and faster speed give every class path higher minimum and average damage than Wooden Club.

blocks.h2: Max your Beginner skills by level 10

blocks.p: You earn 9 SP by the time you hit level 10 (1 per level-up, 9 level-ups from 1 to 10). That's exactly enough to max all three Beginner skills (3 SP each, 9 total).

table: 40 fixed damage, ranged. Consumes 1 Red Snail Shell + 5 MP per cast.

ul: **Nimble Feet**: use the short speed boost to travel between maps or reach monsters. It has a 3-minute cooldown.
**Three Snails**: ranged fixed damage. The shell and MP cost depend on skill level; at max level it uses a Red Snail Shell and 5 MP for 40 damage.
**Recovery**: activate it to recover HP over 30 seconds. At max level it restores 72 HP for 15 MP, with a 2-minute cooldown.

blocks.p: Order matters for levels 1 to 9; by 10 they're all maxed anyway. Take Nimble Feet first, then Three Snails for ranged, Recovery last.
Stick to the Lith Harbor beginner quests until you hit level 10, then head to one of four towns:

ul: Perion: Warriors (Dances With Balrog)
Ellinia: Magicians (Grendel the Really Old)
Henesys: Bowmen (Athena Pierce)
Kerning City: Thieves (Dark Lord)

blocks.p: **Taxis are 90% off while you are still a Beginner.** Ride to your job's town before you advance.

**Don't spend AP on the wrong stat thinking advancement will fix it.** 1st job has no stat requirements (a 4-INT Beginner can advance to Warrior), but your AP does not reset on advancement. Every misallocated point follows you into your job. The only way to undo it is a cash-shop AP Reset.

Every character starts with 4 in each stat. You place 9 more AP at character creation, then get 5 AP per level for STR, DEX, INT, and LUK. Safe split for new players: all of it in your primary until level 10.

ul: Warrior: STR
Magician: INT
Bowman: DEX
Thief: LUK

blocks.p: Potions are most of what you spend mesos on early. Mobs drop them rarely, so buy the ones that restore the most per meso:
Mina's shop in Lith Harbor sells Meat and Lemons. The item efficiency tool ranks every HP and MP item.

ul: **Train where you kill in one or two hits.** Every extra hit costs MP and gives the monster another chance to hit you. If a mob takes three hits, move to weaker mobs until your next weapon.
**Higher skill levels cost more MP.** Energy Bolt goes from 8 MP at level 1 to 16 at max. Power Strike goes from 4 to 12. A level that doesn't save a hit on your map only raises the cost.
**Rest when you run low.** Sit in your chair to refill HP. Switch to basic attacks when MP is low; they cost no MP.
**Gloves and capes are never sold at NPC shops.** They come from drops, crafting, quests, and other players.

blocks.h2: From level 10 to 30: follow your class guide

blocks.p: Lv 10 to 30 is the long middle. The right path depends on the class you picked, so the rest is in the per-class guides:

MapleStory Classic Magician Build and Leveling Guide: Lv 1-30
MapleStory Classic Bowman Build and Leveling Guide: Lv 1-30
MapleStory Classic Thief Build and Leveling Guide: Lv 1-30

blocks.p:
Lv 30 is 2nd job. Same town, same instructor, and you pick a branch:
• **Warrior**: Fighter, Page, Spearman
• **Magician**: Cleric, Ice/Lightning, Fire/Poison
• **Bowman**: Hunter, Crossbowman
• **Thief**: Assassin, Bandit
The class tier list breaks down each branch.

At level 12 you can become a citizen of Henesys or Kerning City. Daily and weekly town quests earn contribution. Each citizen grade raises your discount: 5% to 25% off shops, taxis, and services in your town, and up to 50% off storage. Your class guide recommends a town. The citizenship page lists every grade.

blocks.h2: Quests worth doing from level 10 to 35

blocks.p: These chains reward potions and gear on top of EXP. Rewards are totals for the whole chain.

table: 15x Lemon, 15x Cake, Work Gloves, 2x Return Scroll to Kerning City, 513 EXP, 876 mesos. Nella charges 1,000 mesos to start.
10x Blue Potion, Weighted Earrings or Yellow Square (random), 3,701 EXP, 1,420 mesos
1 random weapon Attack Scroll: Intermediate (one of 14 weapon types), 2,021 EXP, 585 mesos
15x Blue Potion, Old Raggedy Cape, 4,836 EXP, 1,344 mesos
30x Blue Potion, 30x Mana Elixir, 23 return scrolls, 12,486 EXP, 12,046 mesos

blocks.p: COT2 cut many consumable and material sell-back values, so random equipment drops matter more than they look. These early weapon drops sell back for:
**The number above is the NPC sell-back price.** Keep one upgrade you can use, then check duplicates in Safe to Sell? for quest and crafting uses before vendoring them.
Party kills give a bonus on top of the EXP each member earns, and the bonus grows with party size up to four members. The same table sits in the EXP table guide.

ul: **The bonus stops growing at four.** Four, five and six members all get 30%. Extra members still add kill speed.
**Keep swinging.** A member who has not attacked for 15 seconds stops receiving party EXP until they attack again.
**Party up.** Classic gives bonus EXP for party kills, and most early quests are faster with two or three people.
Don't sell quest items. The quest tracker lists which inventory items are needed for active quests so you can check before clearing junk.

**Keep your ores and ETC items.** Crafting opens at level 10. Many recipes start from common drops: 5 Leather make 1 Processed Leather, and 10 Pig's Ribbons make 1 Processed Cloth. Safe to Sell? shows which quests and recipes use each item, and Crafting lists every recipe.

blocks.p: Visit the same maps often enough and you'll start recognizing the other players doing the same. That's how parties form.
